newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends higher on soybean gains, acreage.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends higher on soybean gains, acreage.

text.p: CBOT corn futures ended higher, boosted by a strong showing in CBOT soybeans and ideas that Monday's USDA prospective plantings report would show only a slight increase in corn acreage, traders said.
"The corn is just keying off the wheat and soybeans," said one floor trader.
Floor sources noted commercial short covering ahead of Monday's acreage and grain stocks report.

Analysts expected Monday's report to show corn plantings at 80.92 million acres, above last year's total of 79.49 million acres. But some sources said recent gains in soybeans would "buy" soybean acres away from corn.
Trade was said to be thin ahead of the long Easter weekend and ahead of the report with few traders willing to establish new positions.
The USDA early Thursday reported net weekly corn sales of 569,500 tonnes, within trade estimates for 400,000 to 700,000.
"We saw a lot of people evening out positions in the options pit," an options trader said of Thursday. "Big volumes today but I don't think much of it was new positions."
Corn ended three to 1-1/2 cents per bushel higher with May up three at $3.08-1/4.
News that China sold 87,500 tonnes of corn to South Korea limited gains but some trade sources pointed to reports China may not offer much more corn until the middle of the year.

Traders in China and Hong Kong said a variety of glitches apparently hit exports. Traders cited railway logjams that interrupted the flow of corn toward ports and said export licenses were hard to come by.
Commercials and funds were on both sides of the market. On the day, Cargill sold three million bushels May but also bought three million May, traders said.
Refco Inc sold five million July and two million May early but bought two million May, one million July and two million December later in the session.
Options trade was said to be very active as traders hedged futures positions in the options.
ADM bought 1,800 July $2.60 puts at 1-3/8 to 1-1/2 cents, traders said. One options trader said the purchase covered a previous sale and was not a new position.
Tenco Inc sold 800 May $3.00 puts and 800 May $3.20 calls and 4-1/2 to 5-1/4 cents, floor sources said.
Volume was estimated by the CBOT at 65,000 contracts, compared with Wednesday's volume of 50,232 contracts.
